html:
SMTO-FIL-0054 — The drive SMTO was saving to is full

GUID: 1351c94a-2f4f-4c23-9444-aee6d0c836cb
Slug: file-disk-full
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • The computer reported no free space left where SMTO was saving. Some files from this request may have been saved before the space ran out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check how much free space is left on the drive you were saving to, using that computer's file manager. The computer stopped the save because that drive ran out of room, not because of SMTO.
  2. Delete or move your own files you no longer need from that drive, or tell SMTO to save to a different drive with more space. The save can only finish once there is room for everything.
  3. Before trying again, ask SMTO to list the destination folder. Files saved before the drive filled up may already be there, so you only redo what is missing.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes saving and all the files appear at the destination.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't free space by deleting SMTO's data folder or the original files you asked it to copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A filesystem operation failed with ENOSPC (or Windows ERROR_DISK_FULL / ERROR_HANDLE_DISK_FULL) because the target filesystem has no free capacity.

What this means

  • The OS returned ENOSPC or the corresponding Windows disk-full code during a filesystem operation. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The OS returned ENOSPC or the corresponding Windows disk-full code during a filesystem operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact destination's free blocks, available inodes and relevant filesystem allocation limits; byte free-space alone may be insufficient.

How to fix it

  • Check free space and free inodes on the exact target filesystem (for example df -h and df -i on the path in path_context). Free space through authorized cleanup or choose another destination, and inspect changed_paths and residual_paths in the result before repeating so partial results are settled.
  • Inspect capacity on the exact filesystem and use authorized cleanup or a different eligible destination.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended filesystem has the required allocatable capacity and the original operation's partial state is settled.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
